{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R15"],
      "pins": ["R15.1", "R15.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R15 is valued \"24k\" in the netlist, but its LCSC/MPN fields (FRC0805J240TSD, \"24Ω\" in the description) identify a 24 Ω 0805 part. The value field and the selected part disagree.",
      "expected": "A 24 kΩ resistor (value and part consistent) if this is the intended bleed or divider across the ±15 V-class VOUTP/VOUTN rail. A 24 Ω part across tens of volts would dissipate tens of watts, far beyond a 125 mW 0805 rating.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R15\") (value \"24k\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R15\") (pin \"1\") (pintype \"passive\")) ... (node (ref \"R15\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Either the wrong resistance is populated, or the BOM/value label is wrong. A 24 Ω part on the high-voltage split rail would overheat and fail, and would load the rail heavily. A 24 kΩ value would be a light bleed as intended.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["Q3", "U13"],
      "pins": ["Q3.2", "Q3.3", "U13.1", "U13.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "NET0007", "Net-(Q3-G)"],
      "observed": "The LTC4412 ideal-diode controller U13 has VIN (pin 1) on NET0007 (VBUS side) and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V. Q3, the P-channel pass device it drives, has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on NET0007, which is the reverse of the source-on-input orientation.",
      "expected": "For an LTC4412 PowerPath/ideal-diode stage, the P-channel source should be on the input supply (VIN) and the drain on the load (SENSE). That keeps the body diode oriented to block reverse current.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q3\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\")) ... (node (ref \"Q3\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U13\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, `U6`) ... need reverse current protection mostly"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the pass FET is reversed, its body diode may conduct from the +5V rail back toward the USB input, defeating the reverse-current protection the ideal-diode stage is meant to provide.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "R15 is labelled 24 kΩ but its selected part is a 24 Ω resistor across the VOUTP/VOUTN rail, a clear value/part mismatch that would fail if the part is what gets built. Q3 also appears to be oriented opposite to the LTC4412 convention, which is a lower-confidence concern."
}
